messages:
alex: onboarding weirdness on Windows 10/11 with OneDrive roaming profiles. I run `redwoodctl login` and it writes token to `%APPDATA%\\Roaming\\Redwood\\token`, but soon after `redwoodctl local-serve` says token missing. anyone seen OneDrive interfere?
marta: yep. OneDrive sometimes keeps a file in a syncing state (filename.ext) or moves it to `filename.ext.tmp` while syncing; apps reading at that moment can see missing or zero-length files.
ivan: also OneDrive's Files On‑Demand can make files appear as placeholders (reparse points). If token file is not fully downloaded to disk, reads fail with EISDIR or read 0 bytes.
alex: exact logs: `2026-04-02T10:02:12Z warn token not found at C:\Users\alex\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\token` then immediately `2026-04-02T10:02:13Z info token written` after I run `redwoodctl login` in PowerShell. But local-serve started automatically by my dev script and kept failing until I disabled OneDrive.
marta: reproducible steps: enable OneDrive sync for AppData (some IT policies do this), run login, then quickly `type C:\Users\<me>\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\token` in a new shell. Often it's zero bytes or the file is a cloud placeholder.
ivan: workaround: set `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=C:\Users\<me>\.redwood-local` on Windows to keep a local non-roaming path. Or put token in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` which is not synced.
alex: thinking about fix: 1) have redwoodctl write token atomically: write to `token.tmp` then move/rename to `token` (Windows MoveFile is atomic on same volume) to avoid partial reads. 2) detect OneDrive placeholders by checking `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS` or attempt to open with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT? (windows detail). If placeholder, force a fetch or warn.
marta: atomic write will help but OneDrive can still show a placeholder even after rename if the target path is monitored and OneDrive swaps file metadata during upload. But rename is much better than write-in-place.
ivan: also add retry semantics for reading token: on startup if token missing, poll for up to 5s with exponential backoff before erroring, and include a doctor warning when `%APPDATA%` is inside OneDrive directory.
alex: good candidate: `redwoodctl doctor --windows` should check if `%APPDATA%` path contains `OneDrive` or `\OneDrive - ` prefix and warn. We should add that to onboarding docs.
support-bot: KB article created: "Windows OneDrive and roaming profiles can cause token placeholder/missing errors; use REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR or move to %LOCALAPPDATA%" link: https://intranet/docs/dx/onedrive-token-issue
dev-bot: created issue DX-1748: "Windows: OneDrive / Roaming profile causes token placeholder or zero-byte file during sync; make token writes atomic, add read retry + doctor warning" assigned to @ivan P2. :white_check_mark:
marta: also check installer behavior: MSI shouldn't default config dir into roaming if OS policy moves AppData. Consider detecting OneDrive at install and asking user to opt into local-only config.
ivan: I'll prototype atomic-write + 5s retry and add doctor check. i'll include a repro script that toggles OneDrive placeholder behaviour.
alex: thanks folks, this was driving our new hires crazy. will test the PR when ready :raised_hands:
